name: Bitcoin
title: Where all the bitcoin is: supply, halvings, and who holds it
description: Bitcoin's supply is capped at 21 million; about 20.1 million exist. See the halving schedule, the bitcoin held by US spot ETFs and public companies from SEC filings, and an estimate of lost coins.
tagline: 20.10 million of 21 million created. About 2.2 million are held by ETFs and public companies that publish it.

blocks.label: estimate: 3.125 BTC per block at the 10-minute target

counters.label: New bitcoin issued by the protocol (estimate)

blocks.note: Each block creates 3.125 BTC (the block subsidy since the April 2024 halving) and blocks arrive about every 10 minutes by design, so 3.125 ÷ 600 s = 0.0052 BTC a second. This is an estimate: blocks actually arrive at random. Since block 840,000 the average gap has been 596 s (derived from the timestamps of blocks 840,000 and 973,464), so real issuance runs a little faster. Transaction fees are extra and not counted here. The counter shows the target rate multiplied by time, not blocks found. [[core]] [[mempool]]

sections.title: Supply
sections.lede: Bitcoin's rules cap supply at 21 million coins. As of Oct 27, 2026, 20,104,543 had been created, 95.7% of the cap. [[bci]]

items: Annual new supply at current rate
164,250 BTC a year at 144 blocks a day ÷ supply (derived estimate)

blocks.title: Checking supply from the rules
lines: Subsidy: 50 BTC per block, halving every 210,000 blocks. [[core]]
= **20,104,578.125 BTC** if every subsidy was fully claimed (derived).
The API reports 20,104,543.0 BTC created. The gap of about 35 BTC is because some miners claimed less than the full subsidy; the API counts coins actually created. [[bci]]
Adding all 33 eras gives 20,999,999.9769 BTC, the exact cap (the subsidy is rounded down to whole satoshis, so it is just under 21 million).

blocks.note: Holdings are the latest figures each holder has published, so the dates differ (shown in the tables below). The estimate is Chainalysis's June 2020 count of 3.7 million BTC that had not moved for five years or longer, treated as lost; that was a 2020 figure, and some of those coins may simply be held, so the hatched block is a rough estimate. Wallets of exchanges, governments, funds and individuals are not published and sit in "everything else", which is the supply created less the named holders and the lost estimate. Only holdings in SEC filings or issuers' own pages are named; no on-chain "whale" or government-wallet estimates are used. [[chain]] [[bci]]

sections.title: Issuance and the halving
sections.lede: The reward per block halves every 210,000 blocks, about every four years. It is 3.125 BTC now. [[core]]

items: Block 1,050,000 is the next halving (derived from height 973,464) [[mempool]]
Apr 8, 2028 at the recent 596-second average; Apr 11, 2028 at exactly 10 minutes. Block times vary, so this is an estimate

blocks.title: Halving schedule
blocks.note: Actual start dates are the timestamps of the first block of each era (UTC, mempool.space). Future dates assume 10-minute blocks from the chain tip and are estimates. After era 33 (around the year 2140) the reward rounds down to zero. Showing the first ten of 33 eras. [[core]] [[mempool]]

sections.title: US spot bitcoin ETFs
sections.lede: Each fund reports the bitcoin its custodian holds for it. IBIT's figure is from the issuer's page; the others are from their latest quarterly reports to the SEC (Form 10-Q, June 30, 2026). [[ibit]]

blocks.note: IBIT held 734,261 BTC at June 30, 2026 per its 10-Q, against 811,161 BTC on its page for Oct 26, 2026. Other US spot funds (for example the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust, Invesco Galaxy, CoinShares, Franklin and WisdomTree funds) are not in this total. [[ibit]] [[ibit_q]]

sections.title: Public companies
sections.lede: US-listed companies that state their bitcoin in SEC filings. Figures are the latest filed. [[mstr]]

blocks.note: Strategy's figure is from its Form 8-K for Oct 25, 2026 ("approximately"). MARA's 35,577 includes 9,270 BTC it reports as receivable (lent to counterparties). Tesla's 10-Q says most of its digital assets are 11,509 units of bitcoin. Other public holders, companies outside the SEC system and governments are not listed, because no free official figure was checked for them. [[mara]] [[tsla]]

sections.title: Timeline
sections.lede: Protocol milestones, with dates taken from block timestamps (UTC).

items.text: First halving, at block 210,000: the reward falls from 50 to 25 BTC.
Second halving, at block 420,000: 25 to 12.5 BTC.
Third halving, at block 630,000: 12.5 to 6.25 BTC.
iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) is incepted, per the issuer's fund page. US spot bitcoin ETFs begin.
Fourth halving, at block 840,000: 6.25 to 3.125 BTC.
Block 973,464: 20,104,543 BTC created, 95.7% of the cap.
Fifth halving, at block 1,050,000: 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC. Timing depends on block times.
